Munajat-e-Maqbool

Friday

Seventh manzil · supplications 191 to 203(b)

Opening praise

In the name of Allah, the Most Compassionate, the Most Merciful.

We praise You, O best of those in whom hope is placed and most generous of those from whom anything is sought, for teaching us Munajat-e-Maqbool, which brings nearness to Allah, and the supplications of the Messenger. Send perfect blessings upon him for as long as the west and east winds blow, and branches spring from their roots. Then we ask You for what we are about to recite. Ours is to ask, and Yours is to grant acceptance.

How to read

Read this opening invocation before each daily portion. Begin on Saturday, read one portion each day in order, and complete the cycle on Friday.

Swipe right to left to turn the page

In the name of Allah, the Most Compassionate, the Most Merciful.

Supplication191

Relief and renewal through the Quran

O my Lord, O my Lord, O my Lord! O Allah, O Great One, O All-Hearing, O All-Seeing, O You who have neither partner nor minister; O Creator of the sun and the shining moon; O Protector of the distressed, the fearful and the one seeking refuge; O Provider for the small child; O Mender of the broken bone: I call upon You with the plea of one distressed and poor, like the plea of one desperate and afflicted.

I ask You by the places of might in Your Throne, by the keys of mercy in Your Book, and by the eight names written upon the sun's horn, to make the Quran the spring of my heart and the clearing of my sorrow.

Original commentary 191

This supplication particularly mentions the One who provides for the small child, mends broken bones, and hears the pleas of the distressed, needy and desperate. It acknowledges our helplessness and invokes Allah's greatness and His being All-Hearing and All-Seeing in a prayer whose acceptance is beyond doubt. Such words could be spoken by none other than the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace.

Editorial source note

The original commentary’s certainty of acceptance and exclusive Prophetic attribution are not established by the located sources. The report about eight names written on the sun is severely criticised; its unseen claim and promised protection should not be stated as verified. The familiar request concerning the Qur’an at the end has a separate source. See the reference entry for duʿā 191.

Sources and notesFriday · Prayer p. 141 · Composite containing a severely criticized report and a separately attested closing phrase

Zahr al-Firdaws 619 (alternate numbering 650)

Locator: 2/351–352, no. 619. Variant: From 'O Great, All-Hearing, All-Seeing' through 'the eight names written upon the sun's horn'; not the final Quran petition. The critical edition calls the report weak/rejected; al-Suyuti includes it in al-Ziyadat among fabricated reports, with a transmitter-identity qualification noted in the accompanying research. The report contains the eight-name assertion, but ends with a request to name one's need. Its inclusion in a collection does not establish either the assertion or a guaranteed result.

Yusuf Shabbir, research on the eight names on the sun

Locator: Are Allah's eight names imprinted on the sun?. Component: Critical identification of the preceding report. Reports al-Suyuti's fabrication judgement (al-Ziyadat 2/607) and Ibn Iraq's discussion (Tanzih al-Shariah 2/330); notes uncertainty between Abd Allah ibn Qays and Abd al-Aziz ibn Qays. The identity caveat prevents treating the alleged liar's name as settled. The researcher still finds the report's content rejected.

Al-Hakim, al-Mustadrak 1809

Component: Only the final request that the Quran become the heart's spring and clear sorrow. Al-Hakim: sound on Muslim's conditions if Abd al-Rahman's hearing from his father is established; he expressly records disagreement about that hearing. This belongs to the distinct 'Allahumma inni abduka' report; its attribution cannot authenticate the preceding eight-name formula.

Al-Bukhari, al-Tarikh al-Awsat 1327

Locator: al-Tarikh al-Awsat 1327; al-Bazzar 18/130, no. 90. Parallel only: Repetition of 'O Lord' at the beginning. Al-Bukhari: munkar (rejected). The report promises an answer after four repetitions; this compilation has three. It does not establish a prescribed repetition or guaranteed response here.

The claim about eight divine names written on the sun is not established by a reliable source. The original commentary's certainty that these words can only be Prophetic and that acceptance is beyond doubt conflicts with the documented source problems. These assertions represent the original author's view and are not established by the located sources. The independently attested Quran phrase does not validate the whole composite.

Supplication192

Every need laid before Allah

Our Lord, grant us such and such in this world. O Comforter of every lonely one, O Companion of everyone who is alone, O Near One who is never far, O Witness who is never absent, O Victor who is never overcome; O Ever-Living, O Sustainer, O Possessor of majesty and honour; O Light of the heavens and the earth, O Adornment of the heavens and the earth, O Pillar of the heavens and the earth, O Originator of the heavens and the earth; O Upholder of the heavens and the earth, O Possessor of majesty and honour,

O Responder to those who cry for help, O Final Refuge of those who seek protection, O Reliever of the distressed, O Comforter of the sorrowful, O Answerer of the prayers of the desperate, O Remover of anguish, O God of all worlds, O Most Merciful of the merciful: every need is laid before You.

Original commentary 192

In this supplication, one is taught to ask for worldly needs with the words 'such and such'. While reciting them, picture lawful desires: health and well-being, the welfare of family and children, ample lawful sustenance, and above all a good ending to life. Ask for every need besides these as well. Here, Allah's greatness and majesty are invoked in this appeal: O Helper of those who cry for help, O Acceptor of the pleas of people caught in distress, O Answerer of the prayers of the restless, O Most Merciful of the merciful: I present all my needs to You; accept them according to Your promise.

Sources and notesFriday · Prayer p. 143 · Composite of severely weak or rejected reports with an untraced opening placeholder

Ibn Asakir, Mujam al-Shuyukh 245

Locator: 1/213–214, no. 245. Component: 'O Comforter of every lonely one' through the invocation of the Originator of the heavens and earth, with variant order. Ibn Asakir: isnad wahi (very feeble chain). A report involving a claimant to extraordinary longevity; the associated two-rakah procedure is not established.

Al-Tabarani, al-Mujam al-Awsat 145

Locator: 1/52, no. 145. Variant: The heavens-and-earth invocations and the appeals for relief in the latter portion. Al-Haythami, Majma al-Zawaid 10/181: Salam al-Tawil is abandoned. There are variants in 'Upholder', the seekers of refuge, and the last line.

Al-Dulabi, al-Kuna wal-Asma 1205

Locator: 2/685, no. 1205. Variant: The latter invocations, including 'every need is laid before You'. Al-Albani, al-Silsilah al-Daifah 6218: munkar (rejected). This version provides the closing wording; it is not an authenticating witness for the composite.

The opening 'Our Lord, grant us such and such in this world' was not traced as a specific hadith and is a placeholder for personal needs. It is not a verbatim quotation of Quran 2:201. The three narrative sources do not establish a special ritual, fixed response, or sound Prophetic attribution for the full prayer.

Supplication193

Mercy, character and divine help

O Allah, You are the mighty Creator. You are All-Hearing, All-Knowing. You are Most Forgiving, Most Merciful. You are Lord of the mighty Throne. O Allah, You are the Beneficent, the Bountiful, the Generous. Forgive me, have mercy on me, grant me well-being, provide for me, cover my faults, mend my shortcomings, raise me, guide me, and do not let me go astray. Admit me to Paradise through Your mercy, O Most Merciful of the merciful.

Make me beloved to You, my Lord; make me humble before You within myself; and in the eyes of people, honour me. Keep me away from bad character. O Allah, You have asked of our souls what we possess no power over except through You. Grant us of it that which makes You pleased with us.

Original commentary 193

Every phrase of this supplication is worthy of being constantly on one's lips. It asks for forgiveness, mercy, well-being, ample provision, concealment of sins, and concludes with these words: O Allah, grant us the ability to do the deeds with which You are pleased. It also teaches us to pray: O Allah, I am a great sinner; cover my faults and preserve my honour. It also asks: O Allah, grant us guidance, save us from misguidance, and grant us Paradise through Your grace and mercy. It includes this request that accords with human nature: O Allah, make me honoured in the eyes of people. This is a wonderful supplication.

Supplication193(a)

Lasting faith and well-being

O Allah, I ask You for lasting faith. I ask You for a humble heart. I ask You for true certainty. I ask You for an upright religion, and I ask You for well-being free from every affliction. I ask You for lasting well-being, gratitude for well-being, and independence from people.

Original commentary 193(a)

This supplication asks for sound faith, a heart filled with humility, true certainty, and safety from every affliction. It asks not merely for safety, but for safety that endures. Its final words teach us to pray: O Allah, save me from dependence on Your creation. The request, "I ask You for lasting well-being," means: O Allah, grant us peace and security that are not temporary but enduring. May Allah, exalted is His glory, accept this for all of us.

Locator: Nawadir al-Usul, asl 217 (3/40–41); Kanz al-Ummal 5055. Excerpt: All eight requests, extracted from a ten-request version. The primary compilation supplies no authentication; IslamQA research no. 160411 judges the narrative fabricated, identifying Umar ibn Abi Umar in the chain. The compilation omits the longer version's beneficial-knowledge and complete-well-being requests. Kanz's 'Amr ibn Abi Amr' is discussed as a transcription of Umar ibn Abi Umar.

The requests themselves are distinct from the attached Abu Dharr/Jibril story and its promised rewards. The formula's full Prophetic attribution is not established as authenticated. The much shorter Abu al-Darda prayer in entry 198 has its own separate source and assessment.

Supplication193(b)

Forgiveness for repeated faults

O Allah, I ask Your forgiveness for the sins from which I repented to You but to which I then returned. I ask Your forgiveness for the pledge I gave You concerning myself, then failed to fulfil. I ask Your forgiveness for the blessings through which I gained strength to disobey You. I ask Your forgiveness for every good deed in which I intended Your countenance, but into which something not meant for You became mixed. O Allah, do not disgrace me, for You know me well; and do not punish me, for You have power over all things.

Original commentary 193(b)

This supplication portrays human weakness with great truth and candour: O Allah, I repent again and again, then break my repentance again and again, and fall into the same sins. It contains a remarkable prophetic prayer grounded in reality, whose meaning is: O Allah, I benefit from the blessings You have given me, then use those blessings only to disobey You; forgive me. It also expresses another plain truth: O Allah, I perform good deeds with the intention of pleasing You alone, but afterwards other motives become mixed into them. I ask Your forgiveness for that.

Sources and notesFriday · Prayer p. 148 · Report with unestablished Prophetic attribution and severe source cautions

Locator: 2/617, no. 754; compare Kanz al-Ummal 5126. Variant: All requests; the final clause in the report is 'You have power over me'. Al-Suyuti includes it in al-Ziyadat ala al-Mawduat; Ibn Iraq, Tanzih al-Shariah 2/333, says the chain contains people he did not recognize. The full primary text includes the blessings used in disobedience clause. Its story attributes the formula to al-Khidr and instructs the Companions to use it; that story is not authenticated.

The final 'over all things' is a compilation variant of 'over me' and is retained in this edition. The original commentary explicitly calls this a Prophetic prayer, but the attribution remains unresolved and its transmission is severely criticized.

Sufficiency in pressing matters

O Allah, Lord of the seven heavens and Lord of the mighty Throne, O Allah, be sufficient for me in every pressing matter, however You will and from wherever You will.

Supplication195

Allah's sufficiency in life and the Hereafter

Allah is sufficient for me in my religion. Allah is sufficient for me in my worldly life. Allah is sufficient for me in what concerns me. Allah is sufficient for me against whoever wrongs me. Allah is sufficient for me against whoever envies me. Allah is sufficient for me against whoever plots evil against me. Allah is sufficient for me at death. Allah is sufficient for me when questioned in the grave. Allah is sufficient for me at the Scales. Allah is sufficient for me on the Bridge. Allah is sufficient for me; there is no god but Him. In Him I have placed my trust, and He is Lord of the mighty Throne.

Original commentary 195

This supplication appeals by the seven heavens and the mighty Throne and mentions all the important concerns of this world and the Hereafter. It asks: O Allah, be sufficient for me in all these matters: in my religion and worldly life, at my death, when questioned in the grave, at the scales of justice and on the Bridge. In other words, protect me in all these affairs of this world and the Hereafter. This is a deeply admirable supplication and one of my most beloved prayers.

Supplication196

The company and qualities of the righteous

O Allah, I ask You for the reward of the thankful, the hospitality granted to those brought near to You, the companionship of the prophets, the certainty of the utterly truthful, the humility of the God-fearing, and the humble devotion of those with certainty, until You cause me to die in that state, O Most Merciful of the merciful.

Original commentary 196

The supplication above asks for conviction like that of the friends of Allah and the utterly truthful, humility like that of the God-fearing, and deeds like those of His grateful servants. It pleads that Allah, blessed and exalted is He, grant the companionship of the noble prophets solely through His grace and generosity. It also asks: O Allah, let my life end upon this same faith and certainty. This is an excellent supplication for attaining a good end.

Supplication197

Admission to Paradise through mercy

O Allah, I ask You by Your earlier blessing upon me, by the good trial with which You have tested me, and by Your favour bestowed upon me, to admit me to Paradise through Your kindness, bounty and mercy.

Original commentary 197

This supplication appeals to Allah, exalted is His glory, through His blessings, to which every particle of a person bears witness. It asks: O Allah, every trial and kindness from You surely contains goodness and benefit. In our helplessness and powerlessness, we ask You to admit us to Paradise through Your sheer grace and generosity.

Supplication200

Forgiveness, wholesome earnings and contentment

O Allah, forgive my sin, make my character generous, make my earnings wholesome, and make me content with what You have provided. Do not turn my seeking towards anything You have kept from me.

Original commentary 200

This supplication asks for forgiveness of sins, breadth of character, lawful provision and contentment. Alongside these, the prophetic supplication teaches us to ask: O Allah, whatever is not in my destiny, remove the longing and desire for it from my heart. On contentment, I quote Maulana Abdul Majid Daryabadi: "Whoever possesses the wealth of contentment has no need of the wealth of the seven realms." Glory be to Allah.

Supplication202

Freedom from the Fire and help at death

O Allah, I ask You to free my neck from the Fire. O Allah, help me through the overwhelming pangs of death and its agonies.

Original commentary 202

This supplication teaches us to seek deliverance from the Fire. Who could be prepared to bear the punishment of Hell? Together with this prayer, it especially teaches us to ask for our faith to be protected during the agonies of death, when life is leaving us. The lesson is that the sole means of escaping punishment in the grave and Hell is to carry our faith safely to the grave. May Allah grant us all an end in faith.

Supplication203(a)

Protection from hidden shirk and harm

O Allah, I seek refuge in You from knowingly associating anything with You, and I ask Your forgiveness for what I do not know. I seek refuge in You from a relative whose ties I have severed praying against me. O Allah, I seek refuge in You from the evil of whatever moves on its belly, the evil of whatever walks on two legs, and the evil of whatever walks on four.

Original commentary 203(a)

After seeking protection from associating partners with Allah, this supplication teaches a particularly important lesson that people neglect to put into practice. It is this: O Allah, I seek refuge in You from any relative whose rights I have violated praying against me.

Al-Tabarani, al-Mujam al-Kabir 4849; Abu al-Shaykh, Akhlaq al-Nabi 511

Locator: al-Kabir 5/131, no. 4849; Akhlaq al-Nabi 3/60, no. 511. Component: Only the refuge from a relative whose ties were cut praying against the supplicant. Al-Daraqutni: isolated transmission through Khalid ibn al-Qasim; Ibn Hajar's Lisan al-Mizan 3/334 records adverse criticism of Khalid. Al-Tabarani presents this as Zayd ibn Thabit's bedtime prayer. Abu al-Shaykh's version attributes it to the Prophet; these are distinct levels of attribution.

Ibn Hajar, Lisan al-Mizan 3/334

Locator: 3/334, Khalid al-Madaini. Component: Critical assessment of the preceding kinship petition's transmission. Ibn Hajar records the criticism of Khalid; the source index labels the chain weak. The criticism concerns the version attributed to the Prophet. Al-Haythami gives a positive assessment of the separate report of Zayd ibn Thabit's own prayer.

Al-Haythami, Majma al-Zawaid 10/128

Locator: 10/128, report of Zayd ibn Thabit's bedtime prayer. Component: The kinship request as Zayd ibn Thabit's own supplication, not as a Prophetic report. Al-Haythami: good chain. The text adds a request for sufficiency in family and dependants before the kinship request. Its positive assessment applies to the Companion attribution.

Al-Tabarani, al-Mujam al-Awsat 9304

Locator: al-Awsat 9304; Dalail al-Nubuwwah 150; al-Daawat al-Kabir 363. Component: All three final requests concerning creatures that move on their belly, two legs or four. Al-Haythami, Majma al-Zawaid 1/208: the chain contains Sad ibn Tarif, accused of fabrication. The prayer is part of a bird-and-snake narrative; that incident and its attribution are not established by this chain.

The opening is graded sahih. The kinship request also occurs in Zayd ibn Thabit's own prayer with a chain graded good by al-Haythami, while its attribution to the Prophet is criticized. The animal-protection requests have a separate, severely criticized transmission.

Supplication203(b)

Protection in family, faith and death

O Allah, I seek refuge in You from a wife who makes me grey before old age. I seek refuge in You from a child who becomes a burden upon me, and I seek refuge in You from wealth that becomes a punishment for me. O Allah, I seek refuge in You from doubting the truth after certainty. I seek refuge in You from Satan, the accursed, and I seek refuge in You from the evil of the Day of Judgement.

O Allah, I seek refuge in You from sudden death, the bite of a snake, a wild beast, drowning, burning, falling upon something, and being killed while fleeing from battle.

Original commentary 203(b)

This supplication asks for protection in relation to one's wife, children and wealth. It also warns that, although one's family is a source of comfort, it can sometimes become a great source of trouble and distress. It therefore teaches this prayer: O Allah, do not make my family a source of difficulty for me. In the present world, wealth and children are a great trial; may Allah grant us all success in facing it. This prayer also teaches us to ask: O Allah, protect us from the evil of accidental deaths, drowning, burning, and other calamities and afflictions.

Sources and notesFriday · Prayer p. 157 · Composite with disputed, ungraded and weak transmissions

Al-Tabarani, al-Dua 1339

Locator: 1339; al-Albani, al-Silsilah al-Sahihah 3137. Variant: The first three petitions about spouse, child and wealth. Al-Albani: good chain. Muhammad Amr Abd al-Latif disputes the raising of this report to the Prophet; see the following source. This route has zawj ('spouse') and rabban ('a master over me'), while the compilation has imraah and wabalan ('a burden').

Hannad, al-Zuhd; Abu Said al-Ashajj, Hadith 69

Locator: al-Zuhd 2/505; Hadith Abi Said al-Ashajj 69, p.149; Tarikh Dimashq 17/107. Variant: The family and wealth requests in the opening. Al-Suyuti calls the relevant Sa'id al-Maqburi transmission mursal; Muhammad Amr Abd al-Latif regards this Dawud attribution as the correct form. The earlier form reports Said al-Maqburi recounting a prayer of Dawud. It is not a connected report from Muhammad and includes the anthology's wabalan (burden) variant.

Muhammad Amr Abd al-Latif, Tabyid al-Sahifah

Locator: 1/36; research answer 310963. Component: Authentication dispute over the opening's attribution. Muhammad Amr Abd al-Latif: the apparent chain is good, but connecting and raising it is an error; the correct form is Sa'id's report of Dawud's prayer. This criticism of the report's Prophetic attribution differs from al-Albani's positive assessment.

Abu Nuaym, Tarikh Asbahan 2/170

Locator: 2/170; al-Daraqutni, Atraf al-Gharaib 1/273. Component: The middle three petitions against doubt after certainty, Satan and the evil of Judgement Day. Al-Daraqutni notes the solitary transmission through Jabir al-Jufi; no overall soundness judgement established in the opened record. The primary text matches this section. A singular-transmission observation is not a declaration of authenticity.

Musnad Ahmad 6594 and 17818

Locator: 6594 (11/168); 17818 (29/352). Variant: The final list of seven modes of death. Shuayb al-Arnaut: weak chain. The source describes the Prophet seeking protection from these deaths; the compilation recasts the description as a first-person prayer and omits 'something falling on him'.

The whole passage is not one hadith and cannot receive a single authenticity grade. Its opening has differing scholarly assessments; the middle transmission has the limitations stated above, and the final seven-deaths report is weak.

A humble appeal

From the original edition

At the conclusion of these supplications, I request that you pray that Allah, exalted is His glory, accept every prayer recited in these seven portions on behalf of the following people:

Hakim al-Ummat, Hazrat Maulana Muhammad Ashraf Ali Thanwi, may Allah have mercy on him (author of the book); the late Maulana Abdul Wasi (translation supervisor); the late Maulana Hakim Muhammad Mustafa (first translator); the late Maulana Muhammad Ali; the late Maulana Shabbir Ali; the late Mufti Muhammad Hasan Amritsari; the late Haji Ghulam Sarwar; the late Maulana Abdul Majid Daryabadi; Mr Khalil Ahmad; Dr Abdul Muqeem; all my teachers, spiritual guides and friends; and all believing men and women.

In need of your prayers,
The humble Haﬁz Fazlur Rahim, may Allah pardon him
Deputy Head, Jamia Ashraﬁa, Lahore

ClosingDurood

O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad, the unlettered Prophet, and upon his family, and grant them peace in abundance.

Note from the Urdu edition

Recite Durood at the beginning and end of every manzil. This is a means for supplications to be accepted. (See page 64 of the original edition.)

Reference review

The source’s instruction is retained above. Praise and blessings before duʿā have support in Abu Dawud 1481; the weekly arrangement is the compiler’s. The specific eighty-year reward quoted with Monday’s Durood has not been established as sound. See general references G1 and G3.

General blessings upon the Prophet are supported by Qur’an 33:56. A general encouragement does not by itself establish a particular count, occasion or reward.
